BCP 2021 Section 102.4 states that codes and standards referenced in the code are considered part of the requirements to the prescribed extent of each reference. BCP also states that local, provincial and federal laws are not nullified by the code. Therefore PumpDesign AI should use the 2021 IPC as the default building-plumbing reference when the BCP/AHJ framework calls for IPC. text: BCP Chapter 29 states that the chapter and the International Plumbing Code govern the design, construction, erection and installation of plumbing components, appliances, equipment and systems in buildings covered by the code. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  building_plumbing Pakistan building_plumbing

BCP Table 2902.1 establishes minimum plumbing fixture counts by occupancy. For an apartment house, the table includes one water closet, one lavatory and one bathtub/shower per dwelling unit, plus a kitchen sink per dwelling unit and an automatic clothes-washer connection per 20 dwelling units. Fixture counts are not the same as pump design flow; pump flow must be determined using the applicable hydraulic demand method. text: BCP requires consideration of the AHJ and other applicable laws. Where a specific requirement conflicts with a general requirement, BCP §102.1 states that the specific requirement applies; different applicable requirements may also be subject to the most restrictive provision. PumpDesign AI must therefore record the selected jurisdiction/AHJ and the basis for each governing criterion. IPC §604.3 requires the building water distribution system and pipe sizes to be selected so that, under peak demand, fixture supply outlets provide at least the capacities specified in Table 604.3. Examples include private lavatory 0.8 gpm at 8 psi, shower 2.5 gpm at 8 psi, residential sink 1.75 gpm at 8 psi, and close-coupled tank water closet 3 gpm at 20 psi. Manufacturer requirements govern fixtures not listed. PumpDesign AI should use the pressure requirement of the hydraulically critical fixture/outlet as a terminal-pressure input rather than inventing a generic building pressure. PumpDesign AI should therefore use the minimum credible source pressure when source-pressure data are variable. IPC §604.1 requires water-distribution design to conform to accepted engineering practice and states that methods used to determine pipe sizes must be approved. Appendix E describes water-piping sizing procedures based on minimum static source pressure, head changes caused by friction and elevation, and fixture flow rates. Appendix E is not mandatory unless adopted or referenced by the applicable jurisdiction. text: IPC §602.3.2 states that the combined capacity of the source and storage in an individual water-supply system must supply fixtures at the rates and pressures required by the chapter. Where pumps are installed in basements, the cited provision requires mounting at least 18 inches above the basement floor. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  submersible_pump International / referenced by BCP 2021 submersible_pump

IPC §607.2 states that developed length of hot or tempered water piping from the hot-water source to fixtures requiring hot or tempered water shall not exceed 50 ft; recirculating-system piping and heat-traced piping are considered sources of hot or tempered water. This criterion affects hot-water distribution layout and the need for recirculation. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  hot_water_recirculation International / referenced by BCP 2021 hot_water_recirculation

IPC Chapter 6 requires potable-water systems to be protected against contamination and backflow. PumpDesign AI should flag backflow protection and cross-connection requirements where the pump arrangement or source creates a potential hazard. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  all_potable_water_pumps International / referenced by BCP 2021 all_potable_water_pumps

The February 2023 Punjab criteria recommends a conventional 25-year design period for water-supply networks and states that rising-main sizing is based on maximum-day demand, while distribution-system capacity is based on peak-hour demand. This is a public water-supply criterion and should not automatically be transferred to internal building plumbing. GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED WATER_SUPPLY WATER_SUPPLY PRESSURIZED  public_water_supply Punjab, Pakistan public_water_supply

The 2023 Punjab criteria states that per-capita water supply should be selected considering local water availability, source distance, CAPEX/OPEX and affordability. It provides guideline values by population range rather than a single universal value. PumpDesign AI should therefore require the applicable project/AHJ demand basis instead of hard-coding one Punjab-wide per-capita value for all building projects. GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED WATER_SUPPLY WATER_SUPPLY PRESSURIZED  public_water_supply Punjab, Pakistan public_water_supply

The Punjab 2023 criteria specifies maximum-day demand as 1.5 times average-day demand and peak-hour demand as 1.5 times maximum-day demand or 2.25 times average-day demand. These factors are for the criteria's water-supply system context and must not be assumed for internal building pump sizing when IPC/AHJ fixture-diversity methods govern. GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED WATER_SUPPLY WATER_SUPPLY PRESSURIZED  public_water_supply Punjab, Pakistan public_water_supply

The Punjab 2023 criteria advises at least 12 m minimum terminal pressure in urban areas and at least 8 m in rural areas for the referenced water-supply network context. Treat this as a public-network criterion, not a universal building-fixture residual-pressure rule. GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED WATER_SUPPLY WATER_SUPPLY PRESSURIZED  public_water_supply Punjab, Pakistan public_water_supply

For tubewells, the Punjab 2023 criteria states that tubewells are designed to meet maximum-day demand and recommends an entrance velocity of 0.05 ft/s in the strainer to reduce fine-sand entry. It also states that house-pipe diameter is based on the tube-well design discharge. The Punjab 2023 criteria specifies Hazen-Williams as the head-loss method for pipelines and provides roughness C values of 130 for uPVC/HDPE and 110 for DI/MS in its water-supply context. These values must be stored as source-specific criteria, not universal material constants for every building-pipe product. The Punjab 2023 criteria lists HDPE PE-100 to ISO 4427 / DIN 8074/8075 and identifies pressure classes by application; it also lists ductile iron and mild-steel options for larger mains. Material selection in PumpDesign AI should therefore be tied to the actual product standard, pressure class, internal diameter and project application rather than only a nominal material name. GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED WATER_SUPPLY WATER_SUPPLY PRESSURIZED  public_water_supply Punjab, Pakistan public_water_supply

The Punjab 2023 criteria identifies non-return valves on tube-well delivery arrangements and air-release/air-suction valves at summits and at specified intervals in long rising mains, subject to design and topography. PumpDesign AI should therefore consider air management and non-return valves as system components when designing long rising mains. The February 2023 Punjab criteria notes that an older WASA Lahore design criterion used 80 GPCD, but the 2023 Punjab revision states that continuing to apply a single 80 GPCD value is not appropriate for all localities and instead recommends selecting per-capita supply with local resource, cost and service considerations. PumpDesign AI should not use 80 GPCD as a default merely because it is associated with historical WASA Lahore criteria. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  context_only Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan context_only

IPC §606.5.1 states that where pressure in the public water main or individual water-supply system is insufficient to supply the code-required minimum pressures and quantities, the supply is to be supplemented by an elevated water tank, hydropneumatic pressure booster system, or water pressure booster pump installed in accordance with the code. PumpDesign AI should therefore select the booster arrangement from the project hydraulic conditions and applicable design requirements rather than assume one fixed configuration. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  booster_pump International / referenced by BCP 2021 booster_pump

IPC §606.5.5 requires a low-pressure cutoff on all booster pumps in a water-pressure booster system to prevent creation of a vacuum or negative pressure on the pump suction side when positive suction pressure is 10 psi (68.94 kPa) or less. PumpDesign AI should flag this control/protection requirement in booster designs. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  booster_pump International / referenced by BCP 2021 booster_pump

IPC §606.5.9 requires vacuum relief protection for water pressure tanks, subject to the stated exception for pressurized captive-air diaphragm/bladder tanks. IPC §606.5.10 requires every pressure tank in a hydropneumatic pressure booster system to have a pressure relief valve set at no more than the tank rating and discharged safely by gravity. These are system-protection requirements, not pump hydraulic sizing equations. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  booster_pump International / referenced by BCP 2021 booster_pump

IPC §604.8 states that where static water pressure within a building exceeds 80 psi (552 kPa), an approved pressure-reducing valve is required to reduce building distribution pressure to not greater than 80 psi static, subject to the stated exceptions. PumpDesign AI should check the calculated/available pressure against this limit when designing a booster system. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  booster_pump International / referenced by BCP 2021 booster_pump

For a building booster, the hydraulic head requirement must be determined from the actual system energy balance: required terminal pressure at the critical fixture, elevation difference, pipe friction, minor losses, equipment losses and available inlet pressure. IPC supplies fixture outlet requirements and the requirement for an approved pipe-sizing method; the numerical pump head calculation itself should be performed by deterministic engineering calculations, not by the language model. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  booster_pump International / referenced by BCP 2021 booster_pump

IPC §607.2.1.2 defines demand recirculation systems and requires controls to start the pump from a user/occupancy/flow signal and to limit the temperature entering the cold-water piping to 104°F (40°C). IPC §607.2.2 addresses return routing when a temperature-actuated mixing valve is used. PumpDesign AI should treat control strategy and return routing as part of recirculation design, not only pump head calculation. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  hot_water_recirculation International / referenced by BCP 2021 hot_water_recirculation

ASHRAE 2023 Handbook—HVAC Applications, Chapter 51 states that hot-water recirculation loops are commonly used where piping is long and hot water is desired quickly at fixtures. Return piping and a circulation device are provided; most systems use circulating pumps. Pump controls may use a return-line thermostat, time switch, or demand/on-demand methods such as manual initiation, flow switches or occupancy sensors. Controls that operate only when needed can reduce heat loss and pumping energy. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  hot_water_recirculation International hot_water_recirculation

text: ASHRAE 2023 Chapter 51 states that for larger hot-water recirculation installations, piping heat losses should be determined from the total length of hot-water supply and return piping and an appropriate heat-loss factor from engineering data or insulation/manufacturer data. The required circulation pump flow is then determined from the total heat loss and the allowable temperature drop: Qp = q/(rho cp Δt). For water, the chapter gives rho about 0.99 kg/L at 50°C and cp = 4186.8 J/(kg·K). The allowable temperature drop is a design input; the example cautions that assuming a 10 K drop means accepting that drop at the last fixture. The pump is then selected to provide the required flow and the pressure/head at that flow is obtained from the pump curve. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  hot_water_recirculation International hot_water_recirculation

metadata.reference: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Applications, 2023, Chapter 51, recirculation pump sizing procedure, SI

text: ASHRAE 2023 Chapter 51 separates recirculation flow sizing from pump pressure selection: after calculating the circulation flow from heat loss and allowable temperature drop, select a pump for that flow and obtain the pressure created at that flow from the pump curve. PumpDesign AI should therefore calculate the loop hydraulic resistance from the actual return/supply circuit and report the pump duty point as required flow at required loop head; it should not infer pump head from heat loss alone. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  hot_water_recirculation International hot_water_recirculation

metadata.reference: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Applications, 2023, Chapter 51, recirculation pump sizing procedure

text: ASHRAE 2023 Chapter 51 states that hot-water supply piping is hydraulically sized using the same pressure-drop principles as cold-water piping, while the piping system should meet peak demand at acceptable pressure loss. It also cautions against oversizing hot-water pipes because larger diameter can increase heat loss, delivery delay and lower flow velocity. For recirculation systems, return piping must be sized for the required circulation flow and acceptable pressure loss using the actual loop layout and selected design method. GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING GOVERNING_CODE PRESSURIZED GENERAL_BUILDING_PLUMBING PRESSURIZED  hot_water_recirculation International hot_water_recirculation

metadata.reference: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Applications, 2023, Chapter 51, Distribution/Pipe Sizing

text: ASHRAE 2023 Chapter 51 notes that recirculation loops keep piping hot and can reduce hot-water delivery time, but they also increase energy use because piping is kept hot. The chapter recommends minimizing the size and length of recirculation piping and controlling circulators to operate only as needed. PumpDesign AI should therefore report the heat-loss basis and control strategy alongside the hydraulic pump duty. PumpDesign AI determines candidate pipe diameter from flow and source-backed criteria; the user should not be required to supply a pipe diameter. Steel uses ASME B36.10 NPS/schedule dimensions. Typical Hazen-Williams C values from ASHRAE Chapter 22 are 140 for new steel and 150 for plastic. Velocity checks are service dependent and must not be reduced to one universal material limit. ASHRAE Chapter 22 states typical C=150 for plastic pipe and copper tubing, C=140 for new steel pipe, and values down to 100 and below for badly corroded or very rough pipe.
